title: CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts
abstract: arXiv:2611.17115v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. We ask whether small language model (SLM) agents can be trusted to write these artifacts. Across 15 open-weight models, 13 of them between 1.7B and 12B parameters, they cannot: the policies, graphs and constraints that the agent's model writes admit attacks on 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) and 11 (DRIFT) of the models, and CaMeL's programs fail to run in up to 68% of episodes. We present CapLite, which derives its policy from the tool schemas, commits the write calls before any tool result is read, and admits a write only if every argument that decides whom or what it affects is stated in the user's request. This guarantees write integrity: injected text cannot add a write, and no write reaches a rec

translated_title: CapLite：无需模型编写安全工件的小语言模型智能体提示注入防御
translated_abstract: 针对提示注入的执行类防御（如 CaMeL、Progent、IPIGuard 和 DRIFT）要求智能体自身的模型来编写一个安全工件（程序、权限策略、依赖图或约束列表），再由代码加以执行。我们探究了小语言模型（SLM）智能体是否能被信任来编写这些工件。在 15 个开源权重模型中（其中 13 个参数量介于 1.7B 到 12B 之间），答案是肯定的“不能”：智能体模型编写的策略、图和约束列表在 14 个（Progent）、13 个（IPIGuard）和 11 个（DRIFT）模型上存在可被攻击的漏洞，而 CaMeL 的程序在多达 68% 的运行回合中无法执行。我们提出了 CapLite，它从工具模式（schema）中推导策略，在任何工具结果被读取之前就提交写调用，并且只有当决定写操作影响对象或内容的每个参数都在用户请求中明确说明时才允许该写操作。这保证了写完整性：注入的文本无法添加写操作，且任何写操作都不会到达被污染的接收者。
tldr: 论文发现小语言模型无法可靠地编写现有提示注入防御（CaMeL、Progent、IPIGuard、DRIFT）所依赖的安全工件，并提出 CapLite——通过从工具模式推导策略、在读取工具结果前提交写调用、且仅允许参数均来自用户请求的写操作，从而无需模型编写安全工件即可保证写完整性的新防御方法。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that small language model agents cannot be trusted to write the security artifacts required by existing prompt-injection defenses (CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard, DRIFT), and proposes CapLite, which derives its policy from tool schemas, commits writes before reading tool results, and admits only writes whose arguments are stated in the user's request, guaranteeing write integrity without model-written security artifacts.
